subject: CareAssist POC alignment: bilingual model shortlist & next steps
content:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: CareAssist POC alignment: bilingual model shortlist & next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the trial kicked off next week: 

Summary of ask
- Use-case: triage + templated response drafts for CareAssist support tickets (English + Spanish).
- Traffic: ~500 daily tickets initially; peak 80 req/min (business hours).
- Success metric: reduce average first-response time and maintain >=88% accuracy on intent classification + >=4.2 quality score on reply drafts (annotated sample).

Proposed POC (4 weeks) — high level
1) Week 0: finalize SOW & enable Redwood Dedicated trial tenant (isolated env).
2) Week 1: ingest 5k anonymized ticket transcripts (English + Spanish) and run baseline eval.
3) Week 2: model tuning, prompt sets, and guarded prompts for PHI handling.
4) Week 3: UAT with sample agents (50 tickets/day) + quality/latency monitoring.
5) Week 4: acceptance & handoff / next-phase pricing discussion.

Model shortlist for the trial (open models) — initial recommendation- Primary: Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized) — good balance of instruction-following and cost for English.- Secondary: Mistral-7B-instruct — competitive quality on short-form generation and lower token cost for routine templates.- Spanish-specific fallback: Llama-2-7b-q4 or mT5-based translation fallback if direct Spanish performance drops below threshold.

Fallback policy
- Route English traffic to primary; Spanish to Mistral where it performs; if generation confidence score < 0.65, then fall back to a smaller quantized model (Llama-2-7b-q4) or use an instruction to translate+generate via mT5 pipeline.

Success criteria (proposal)
- Intent classification: precision >= 0.88 on the annotated holdout set.
- Draft quality: average human rating >= 4.2/5 over 200 sampled replies.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 650ms for 32-token answer (under trial load).
- Cost: token spend <= projected monthly budget (Jordan will include baseline estimate).

Actions / owners
- Jordan Blake (me): coordinate kickoff, commercial paperwork, and weekly check-ins.
- Diego Fernandez (solutions): model evaluation matrix and infra config (batching/caching).
- Marissa Cole (CS): success criteria validation and acceptance testing coordination.
- CareAssist: provide anonymized ticket dump + acceptance reviewers (2 agents).

Attachments: careassist-poc-charter-v1.pdf (charter + timeline).

Proposed next meeting: Thu Jul 16, 10:00am PT to finalize SOW and handoff to procurement. Please confirm availability.

Thanks,

- Data: we can provide 6k anonymized tickets (English + ~25% Spanish). We need assurances on retention/window and a plan for PII/PHI redaction during ingestion.
- Spanish quality: our Spanish testers are sensitive to formality/tone; we’d like to be able to control style (formal vs casual).

On Wed, 15 Jul 2026 at 09:05 AM Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com> wrote:

Hi all — quick technical notes attached (model-eval-matrix.xlsx). Key callouts: 
- For bilingual service we recommend running a small language-detection step (sub-10ms) and routing to a language-optimized prompt per model.
- Quantized Llama-2-13b gives the best quality/latency balance in our infra; for tight cost control we can run a Q4 Llama-2-7b fallback under low-confidence conditions.
- If CareAssist needs strict formality tuning for Spanish, we suggest a lightweight prompt-tuning pass on ~1k curated Spanish replies (can be done inside the 4-week POC).
- Infra config: continuous batching + prefix KV caching; suggested batch target 16 and max latency slot 700ms.

Attachment: model-eval-matrix.xlsx (quality/latency estimates across shortlisted models).

Diego Fernandez

Thanks team — I’ll own acceptance testing and the quality rubric. A couple small updates to the success criteria to keep acceptance objective: 

Acceptance checklist (to be automated where possible)
- Holdout set: 1,000 tickets stratified by intent & language.
- Intent precision >= 0.88 and recall >= 0.80.
- Reply drafts: blind-review by 3 CareAssist agents; median rating >= 4.2 and no more than 6% judged to require significant rewrite.
- Safety: no high-severity PHI exposures in the ingested dataset and system-wide redaction turned on for PII.

Owner assignments
- Test harness + sampling: Marissa Cole (redwood) + CareAssist Ops lead (TBD).
- Model eval & infra tuning: Diego Fernandez.
- Commercial & SOW: Jordan Blake.

I’ll prepare the acceptance rubric doc and upload to the shared Drive before the kickoff.
